title: Hybrid HEC Polling Adapter for SIEM Integrations with SLA-Aware Delivery Guarantees
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: High-throughput tenants experience repeated webhook/DLQ storms when downstream SIEM endpoints (Splunk HEC, Datadog HTTP intake) slow or drop connections. Current push-only forwarders cause amplification of retries and put tenant isolation at risk. Goal: Build a hybrid push/poll adapter for SIEM integrations that preserves ordering where required, provides tenant-scoped idempotency tokens, supports adaptive backpressure, and exposes SLO metrics so Console can show per-tenant SLA attainment. Non-goal: Replacing existing audit storage or changing event schema beyond optional envelope headers.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter supports two modes: push (webhook/HEC) and poll (pull from our reliable queue) selectable per-sink
Per-tenant sequence watermarking is recorded so retried batches are deduplicated by downstream connectors
Retries use jittered, SLA-aware backoff; we unblock best-effort tenants faster while protecting high-SLA tenants
End-to-end telemetry emitted: time-in-queue, send-latency, ack-latency, retry-count, final-delivery-status
Integration tests simulate downstream slowdowns and verify no amplification (<=1.1x event duplication under burst) and bounded queue growth
Console shows per-route SLA attainment and open DLQ items with remediation links
proposed_design: Architecture: introduce an adapter layer between audit-shipper and sink-adapters. The adapter exposes pull endpoints that can be used by a lightweight poller or push directly to HEC/Datadog
Per-tenant watermark: persistent monotonic watermark stored in tenant metadata store; each batch includes a watermark and idempotency token computed from watermark+batch-id
Mode switch: sink config property 'delivery_mode' with values 'push'|'poll'|'hybrid' (hybrid uses push when downstream healthy, falls back to poll on degradation)
Backpressure controller: central rate limiter that takes tenant SLA tier, current queue length and downstream health probes to compute per-tenant allowed concurrency
Retry semantics: at-most-once by default; exactly-once emulation via idempotency tokens and dedupe window for tenants with high SLA
Compatibility shims: Splunk HEC header mapping to include X-Redwood-Watermark and X-Redwood-Idempotency; Datadog intake uses a similar header convention and tag mapping
Observability: span annotations and Prometheus metrics exposed by adapter; events streaming to Console via existing telemetry pipeline
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Full exactly-once would require stronger distributed consensus (too heavy) — we opt for watermark + dedupe window which is pragmatic and operationally measurable
Polling increases latency for some events; hybrid mode mitigates this by keeping push as primary when downstream healthy
Per-tenant state increases metadata storage; we shard tenant watermarks and GC old ones after inactivity to reduce costs
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flags: behind 'siem_hybrid_adapter' feature flag per-tenant and per-route
2) Internal dogfooding: enable for internal test tenants and our security team with Datadog and Splunk test endpoints
3) Canary: enable hybrid mode for 5 low-risk external tenants, monitor metrics for 48 hours
4) Gradual ramp: enable adaptive backpressure for medium-SLA tenants, then high-SLA tenants after verification
5) Public opt-in with clear Console toggle, default remains current push-only behavior for existing tenants
metrics_slos: Per-tenant 99th percentile final-delivery-latency goal: <= 10s for push mode, <= 30s for hybrid under normal load
Duplication rate: <0.5% for high-SLA tenants, <1.5% for best-effort tenants during bursts
Queue growth: when downstream is unhealthy, queue length should plateau and not grow for more than 30 minutes for high-SLA tenants (with autoscaling triggers)
tests_and_validation: Simulated downstream slow: script to add 200ms-5s artificial latency to Splunk HEC and verify adapter falls back to poll mode
Duplication fuzz tests: replay with out-of-order ACKs to ensure watermark dedupe logic holds
Chaos test: kill adapter instances during in-flight batches and validate idempotency handling and GC correctness
Load test: 50k events/sec across 200 tenants with mixed SLA tiers; measure per-tenant fairness and backlog boundedness
